title: Hook
text: If you were falling from the sky without a parachute, would you aim for a deep lake or a dense forest?
nxt: Most people instinctively choose the water, picturing a deep, forgiving dive. But the physics points the other way.

title: Speed
text: A person falling belly-down through the lower atmosphere settles at roughly two hundred kilometers per hour, about fifty-five meters per second.
nxt: At that speed, the surface you meet decides almost everything.

title: Speed
text: At that speed, the surface you meet decides almost everything.
prev: A person falling belly-down through the lower atmosphere settles at roughly two hundred kilometers per hour, about fifty-five meters per second.

title: Water
text: Water is almost incompressible, and it cannot move out of the way fast enough when you strike it at that speed.
nxt: Instead of letting you in gently, it pushes back hard, much like a solid surface.

nxt: Hitting a lake or the ocean flat-on is very often fatal.

title: The Secret Variable
text: The secret variable is stopping distance. When a body stops over a few millimeters, the force is enormous. Lengthen the distance, and the time, and the peak force falls.
nxt: As an illustration, stopping over three meters instead of three centimeters spreads the same energy across a hundred times more distance.

title: Trees
text: That is why dense trees matter. As a body hits the top of the canopy, thin twigs snap first and take a modest share of the energy.
nxt: Then thicker branches bend and break, absorbing much more.

title: Snow
text: Deep, freshly fallen snow can do something similar.
nxt: It is mostly trapped air in a lattice of crystals, so it compresses gradually, like the crumple zone of a car.

nxt: On a steep slope, a head-on impact becomes a glancing blow, and the body slides, shedding speed across distance.

title: Real Survivors
text: Real survivors show the pattern.
nxt: In 1972, flight attendant Vesna Vulovic fell about ten thousand meters with part of her aircraft, and accounts say she came down on a wooded, snowy slope.

nxt: In 1971, Juliane Koepcke fell about three kilometers, still strapped into her seat, into the Peruvian rainforest.

title: Time and Force
text: Stretch an impact from one hundredth of a second to one tenth of a second, and the average force drops to one tenth.
nxt: That is the difference between a stop that breaks a body and one that, with a lot of luck, it can survive.
